clue.text: One of the Fab Four not appearing in Hebridean location

indicators.note: not tells us the following word's letters are dropped from the Beatle's surname

parts.note: George Harrison was one of the Beatles, nicknamed the Fab Four
a show that is appearing is on

explanation.surface: A Beatle is missing from somewhere in the Hebrides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not appearing' works as 'not' (remove) plus 'appearing' (ON), taking ON from the end of the surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Harris is the southern part of the island of Lewis and Harris in the Outer Hebrides, off Scotland's west coast.

clue.text: Transport boss a vacuous type

parts.note: air is a mode of transport, as in travel by air
a head is the boss of an organisation

explanation.surface: The head of a transport firm is an empty-headed sort.
explanation.definitionFit: An airhead is slang for a silly, empty-minded person.

clue.text: Judge it necessary for a makeover

parts.note: a ref, or referee, judges a game

explanation.surface: A judge declares something needs a makeover.
explanation.definitionFit: A refit is a renovation or overhaul, especially of a ship or shop.

clue.text: Most ingratiating sergeant major leading troops close to front

indicators.note: leading puts the sergeant major in front of the troops

parts.note: armies are bodies of troops

indicators.note: close to means the last letter of the word front

explanation.surface: A fawning sergeant major leads the troops up to the front line.
explanation.definitionFit: Smarmy means oily and fawning, and this is its superlative.

clue.text: Stunning ruins of Tangiers

indicators.note: ruins suggests the city's name is wrecked and its letters rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: Something spectacular among the ruins of a Moroccan port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stunning' looks like an adjective praising the ruins, but it is the verb sense: shocking someone with an electric stun gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Using a Taser on someone is stunning them with an electric shock, so the participles match.

clue.text: Having change of heart maybe, I'll leave railway terminal clutching map

indicators.note: clutching means the remaining station holds the map inside it
leave means the letter departs from the station

parts.note: a train station is a railway terminal
I'll reads as I will: the letter I is the one that goes
a plan is a map or diagram

explanation.surface: A traveller changes their mind and leaves the train station with a map in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'll' reads as 'I will': the I is what 'leave' removes, and 'clutching' then holds the map inside the shortened station.
explanation.definitionFit: A heart transplant is the classic example of this surgery, so 'maybe' marks the definition as an example.

clue.text: Brawl towards middle of tennis match, you say?

indicators.note: you say means the phrase is pronounced, not spelt

parts.note: the second set comes towards the middle of a tennis match

explanation.surface: A fight breaks out midway through a tennis match.
explanation.definitionFit: A set-to is a fight or heated argument.

clue.text: Really like old actor's final appearance in smutty show

indicators.note: in places the liking, the old and the final letter inside the smutty word

parts.note: smutty jokes are rude
to dig something is slang for really liking it

indicators.note: final points to the last letter of actor's

explanation.surface: An old actor's last appearance is in a crude show, which he really likes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appearance' is only a link; 'in' places the three pieces inside the smutty word as one run.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruddigore is a Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera, a stage show.

clue.text: Refusal by nurse constituted a form of neglect

parts.note: no is a refusal

indicators.note: constituted suggests the letters are put together in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A nurse's refusal amounts to neglect of a patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link word joining the refusal to the rearranged nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, non-user is the failure to exercise a right, which may then be lost: neglect of a right.

clue.text: After split with leader of Democrats, a group of politicians shortly become estranged

indicators.note: After places the split word directly behind the Democrats' initial
the leader of a word is its first letter, here of Democrats

parts.note: a split is a rift between people

indicators.note: shortly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a political party is a group of politicians

explanation.surface: After a split in the Democratic party, members briefly fall out with one another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' drops the final Y of PARTY to leave PART.
explanation.definitionFit: To drift apart is to grow distant from someone gradually, the same as becoming estranged.

clue.text: Publishing house making little impression

definitions.meaning: J. M. ... is a long-standing London publisher, famous for the Everyman's Library
a small hollow pressed into a surface, as in a car bodywork

explanation.surface: A publisher making little mark on the market.
explanation.definitionFit: One word names both the British publishing firm and a small dint or depression left by a knock.

clue.text: Late accounts from journalist attached to newspaper probing British politicians

indicators.note: probing means pushing into, so the journalist-plus-paper pair goes inside the British politicians

parts.note: Tories are Conservative politicians in Britain

indicators.note: attached to joins the editor directly onto the front of the newspaper's name

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is the crossword's usual journalist
The Times is a London daily newspaper

explanation.surface: A reporter at a newspaper investigates British Conservative MPs.
explanation.walkthrough: The pair EDTIMES slips in after the B, so B ... TORIES is the outer piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Stories read to children at bedtime are tales told late in the day, hence late accounts.

clue.text: Backing bill, Mr Cable ignores new words of wisdom

indicators.note: Backing means the bill stands behind and supports the following word, so it comes first

parts.note: an ad, or advertisement, is a bill posted up

indicators.note: ignores means the next letter is left out of the politician's first name

parts.note: Vince Cable was a Liberal Democrat leader and UK Business Secretary

explanation.surface: Vince Cable supports a bill while ignoring new advice.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping N from VINCE leaves VICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Advice is guidance or counsel, which is what words of wisdom offer.

clue.text: Rash naughty child has got turned nasty

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child

indicators.note: nasty indicates the word is mangled into a different order

explanation.surface: A badly behaved child has turned unpleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nasty' looks like the result of turning, but it is the anagram signal for TURNED.
explanation.definitionFit: Imprudent means unwise or reckless, as is a rash decision.

clue.text: Fat pig entering part of ship

indicators.note: entering means the animal goes inside the cooking fat

parts.note: lard is pig fat used in cooking
a boar is a male pig

explanation.surface: A greasy pig wanders onto a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Larboard is the old name for the port side of a vessel.

clue.text: Gave report about officer being posted elsewhere?

indicators.note: about means the report word wraps round the officer

parts.note: to relate is to tell, so gave report is related
OC stands for Officer Commanding

explanation.surface: Someone reported on an officer being posted away.
explanation.definitionFit: A person relocated has been moved to a new place, as an employee or soldier transferred to another post.

clue.text: Notorious monk outraged puritans

indicators.note: outraged hints that the word is thrown into a disturbed new order

explanation.surface: Strict moralists are scandalised by a notorious monk.
explanation.definitionFit: Grigori Rasputin was the infamous mystic monk who held sway over Russia's last imperial family.

clue.text: In which a fellow and female come together with a passion

definitions.text: In which a fellow and female come together with a passion

parts.note: ire is anger, a passion

explanation.surface: A man and woman meet in a passionate encounter.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay; 'come together' simply joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An affaire, from French affaire de coeur, is a love affair in which two lovers are joined by passion.

clue.text: Songs claimed falsely to be by Queen

parts.note: someone who claimed falsely lied
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword Queen

explanation.surface: Songs were falsely said to be written by the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Lieder are German art songs, such as those by Schubert for voice and piano.

clue.text: Scripture scholar, say, admitted to a university briefly

indicators.note: admitted to means the example goes inside the shortened university name
briefly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: Exeter, in Devon, is a university
e.g., for example, is what 'say' means

explanation.surface: A biblical scholar, for instance, is admitted to a university.
explanation.walkthrough: Exeter, in Devon, is a university town; 'briefly' trims its last letter before 'admitted to' puts the example inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An exegete interprets texts, especially the Bible, so is a scholar of scripture.

clue.text: Lucky mascot following football club supporter onto our field

indicators.note: onto shows the club and supporter pieces are placed after our field

parts.note: F is the standard abbreviation for following, as in page references
a lea is a poetic word for a meadow or field
a lover of something is a fan or supporter

explanation.surface: A lucky charm comes along as a football fan runs onto the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A clover with four leaves instead of three is a rare plant traditionally carried as a good-luck token.

clue.text: See animal getting caught — by this?

definitions.text: See animal getting caught — by this?

indicators.note: getting caught means the animal is held inside the look word

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
an ass is a donkey

explanation.surface: Watch an animal being snared, perhaps with this.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a lasso is the rope that catches an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A lasso is a looped rope thrown to catch cattle or horses.

clue.text: I literally will come last in some games

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words some games

explanation.surface: Someone vows to finish last in certain contests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I literally' means 'I, as a letter': in Revelation God says 'I am the Alpha and the Omega', the first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet, so it literally comes at the end.

clue.text: Ceremony held regularly in Braintree

indicators.note: held regularly in says every other letter inside the town's name is kept

explanation.surface: A ceremony takes place regularly in an Essex town.
explanation.walkthrough: Braintree is a town in Essex; take its 2nd, 4th, 6th and 8th letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A rite is a formal religious or solemn ceremony.

clue.text: School isn't safe for pious fellow

parts.note: ain't is a colloquial form of isn't
peter is old criminal slang for a safe

explanation.surface: A school is not a safe place for a religious man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peter' for a safe comes from thieves' slang; safe-crackers were called peter-men.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostle who became the first bishop of Rome is held up as a holy man.

clue.text: Dismissed by university, dons went berserk

indicators.note: went berserk suggests the two words run wild and their letters scramble

explanation.surface: Academics run amok and get thrown out of the university.
explanation.definitionFit: At British universities a student expelled or suspended is said to be sent down.

clue.text: Bank employee not stressed about losing unknown amount

indicators.note: about suggests the remaining letters are turned round and rearranged
losing means the following letter is dropped from that word

parts.note: someone not stressed is relaxed
X is the usual algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A calm bank worker has misplaced an undisclosed sum.
explanation.walkthrough: RELAXED without X gives RELAED, which 'about' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A dealer works in a bank's trading room buying and selling currencies or securities.
